'''Christopher Murphy Rabb''' (born February 21, 1970)<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.legistorm.com/person/bio/14318/Sharon_Brenna_Findley_Bird.html|title=Chris Rabb - D Pennsylvania, 3rd, Candidate |publisher=legistorm.com |date=2023 |access-date=2026-10-19}}</ref> is an American politician who is the Representative-elect for [[Pennsylvania's 3rd congressional district]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Pennsylvania U.S. House results: 3rd District |url=https://apnews.com/projects/elections-2026/pennsylvania-us-house-results/#3 |access-date=4 November 2026 |website=AP News |publisher=Associated Press}}</ref> A member of the [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic Party]] and the [[Democratic Socialists of America]], he has represented the [[Pennsylvania House of Representatives, District 200|200th District]] in the [[Pennsylvania House of Representatives]] since 2017.

== Early life, family and education ==
[[File:Christopher Rabb 1988.jpg|thumb|left|upright=1.2|Rabb in the [[St. Ignatius College Prep]] yearbook, 1988]]

Rabb was born in Chicago, to an ophthalmologist and professor father, [[Maurice Rabb Jr.]], and a politically active mother, Madeline Murphy Rabb.<ref name ="Meet"/><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.murphyrabb.com/AboutUs/Biography/tabid/739/Default.aspx|title=Biography|date=September 27, 2007|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070927080526/http://www.murphyrabb.com/AboutUs/Biography/tabid/739/Default.aspx|archive-date=September 27, 2007}}</ref> His maternal grandmother, [[Madeline Wheeler Murphy]], was a Baltimore-based community activist, and his maternal grandfather, [[William H. Murphy Sr.]], was a judge in Baltimore.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.thehistorymakers.org/biography/honorable-william-h-murphy-sr|title=The Honorable William H. Murphy, Sr.'s Biography|website=The HistoryMakers}}</ref> Rabb's great-great-grandfather, [[John H. Murphy Sr.]], was born into slavery and founded the ''[[Baltimore Afro-American]]'' in 1892.<ref name ="Meet"/>

Shortly after beginning his undergraduate education at [[Yale University]] in 1988, Rabb was instrumental in the removal of an image of a shackled slave from the common room of [[Grace Hopper College|Calhoun College]] (named after alumnus [[John C. Calhoun]], since renamed after alumna [[Grace Hopper]]). In the process Rabb also learned he was a descendant of [[Philip Livingston]].<ref name="Calhoun">{{cite news|title=What's in a name? Looking for answers at Calhoun College|work=Yale Alumni Magazine|author-first=Carole |author-last=Bass|date=March 19, 2014|url=https://yalealumnimagazine.com/blog_posts/1740-what-s-in-a-name-looking-for-answers-at-calhoun-college}}</ref> Rabb received his bachelor's degree from Yale in 1992.<ref name="Calhoun" /> Rabb received a master's degree in organizational dynamics from the [[University of Pennsylvania]] in 2006.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://votesmart.org/candidate/biography/167968/christopher-rabb#.Wst__Ijwa70|title=Vote Smart|access-date=April 9, 2018}}</ref>

==Career==
[[File:Chris Rabb at National Conference for Media Reform.jpg|thumb|left|upright=1.2|Rabb at the [[National Conference for Media Reform]], June 7, 2008]]

In the early 1990s, Rabb worked as an aide to U.S. Senator [[Carol Moseley Braun]].<ref name ="Meet">{{cite web|url=https://www.inquirer.com/philly/news/politics/20170114_Meet_new_Philly_State_Rep__Chris_Rabb.html|title=Meet new Philly State Rep. Chris Rabb|first=John|last=Baer|website=[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]]|date=January 14, 2017 }}</ref> He then worked for the [[Clinton administration]] in the 1995 [[White House Conference on Small Business]].<ref name ="Meet"/> Since moving to Philadelphia to obtain his master's at Penn, he has taught a business course at [[Temple University]].<ref name ="Meet"/> He published the non-fiction book ''Invisible Capital: How Unseen Forces Shape Entrepreneurial Opportunity'' in 2010.<ref name ="Meet"/>

===Pennsylvania House of Representatives===
In 2016, Rabb defeated the incumbent state representative [[Tonyelle Cook-Artis]], who was supported by the Pennsylvania Democratic establishment,<ref name=":0">{{cite news|url=https://www.phillymag.com/citified/2016/05/19/chris-rabb-interview/|title=The Incredible Political Insurgency of Chris Rabb|work=Philadelphia Magazine|date=May 19, 2016|author-first=Holly |author-last=Otterbein}}</ref> in a three-way Democratic primary 47% to 40%, and then defeated Republican challenger Latryse McDowell 94% to 5% in the November general election.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{cite web|url=https://electionreturns.pa.gov/Home/SummaryResults?ElectionID=63&ElectionType=P&IsActive=0|title=Pennsylvania Elections - Summary Results|website=electionreturns.pa.gov}}</ref> He won the 2018 primary over establishment-backed challenger Melissa Scott 52% to 48%,<ref name="Baer2017">{{cite news |title=Rabb: Budget process 'boggles the mind' |last=Baer |first=John |work=Philadelphia Inquirer |date=October 2, 2017 |page=B1 |id={{ProQuest|1945372538}} }}</ref> and has since run unopposed in 2020 and 2024.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.electionreturns.pa.gov/General/OfficeResults?OfficeID=13&ElectionID=63&ElectionType=G&IsActive=0|title=Pennsylvania Elections - Office Results|website=www.electionreturns.pa.gov}}</ref>

Rabb has been a member of the [[Pennsylvania House of Representatives]], representing the [[Pennsylvania House of Representatives, District 200|200th District]], since 2017.<ref>{{cite web |title=House Session Days |access-date=April 9, 2018 |url=http://www.legis.state.pa.us/SessionDays.cfm?SessionYear=2017&SessionInd=0&Chamber=H}}</ref> Rabb serves on a number of House Committees, including Agriculture & Rural Affairs,<ref name="Caruso">{{cite news |last1=Caruso |first1=Stephen |title=While the state farm bill is a start, Pennsylvania's agriculture leaders see further reforms • Pennsylvania Capital-Star |url=https://penncapital-star.com/labor/while-the-state-farm-bill-is-a-start-pennsylvanias-agriculture-leaders-see-further-reforms/ |access-date=24 September 2024 |work=Pennsylvania Capital-Star |date=8 January 2020}}</ref> Commerce,<!-- Majority Subcommittee Chair on Local Business --><ref name="Peter">{{cite news |last1=Hall |first1=Peter |title=Measure to empower banks to fight financial exploitation of elders passes Pa. House panel • Pennsylvania Capital-Star |url=https://penncapital-star.com/criminal-justice/measure-to-empower-banks-to-fight-financial-exploitation-of-elders-passes-pa-house-panel/ |access-date=24 September 2024 |work=Pennsylvania Capital-Star |date=21 May 2024}}</ref>
<!-- Finance, Majority Subcommittee Chair on Tax Modernization and Reform -->and the Judiciary.<ref name="Hall">{{cite news |last1=Hall |first1=Peter |title=Restorative justice often leads to better outcomes for victims and offenders, experts say • Pennsylvania Capital-Star |url=https://penncapital-star.com/civil-rights-social-justice/restorative-justice-often-leads-to-better-outcomes-for-victims-and-offenders-experts-say/ |access-date=24 September 2024 |work=Pennsylvania Capital-Star |date=30 April 2024}}</ref><ref name="Sweitzer">{{cite news |last1=Sweitzer |first1=Justin |title=Death penalty repeal bill advances in PA House |url=https://www.cityandstatepa.com/policy/2023/10/death-penalty-repeal-bill-advances-pa-house/391660/ |access-date=24 September 2024 |work=City & State PA |date=31 October 2023 |language=en}}</ref> Rabb has put forward bills that would enable courts in the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania to use [[restorative justice]] approaches to sentencing offenders,<ref name="Hall"/><ref name="Lengyel">{{cite news |last1=Lengyel |first1=Christina |title=Restorative justice advocates ask for state-level reform |url=https://www.thecentersquare.com/pennsylvania/article_6dc9a9c2-0976-11ef-a72d-2768f5bb6dba.html |access-date=24 September 2024 |work=The Center Square |date=3 May 2024 |language=en}}</ref> and introduced and passed bills in the Pennsylvania House to repeal the use of the [[death penalty]] (House Bill 999).<ref name="Sweitzer"/>

In 2017, Rabb helped to found the Pennsylvania Climate Caucus.<ref name="NCEL"/><ref>{{cite web |title=HD 200 - Rep. Chris Rabb {{!}} Conservation Voters of Pennsylvania |url=https://www.conservationpa.org/endorsements/hd-200-rep-chris-rabb |website=Conservation Voters of Pennsylvania|date=2020 |language=en}}</ref> 
In 2024, Rabb introduced legislation to counter [[greenwashing]], which is deceptive marketing that incorrectly suggests that a product is beneficial to the environment. According to the Center for Climate Integrity, the bill is the first of its type in the nation.<ref name="Stephens">{{cite news |last1=Stephens |first1=Jenny |title=Democratic Pennsylvania State Representative Chris Rabb to Introduce Landmark Legislation That Takes Aim at Greenwashing - Bucks County Beacon |url=https://buckscountybeacon.com/2024/07/democratic-pennsylvania-state-representative-chris-rabb-to-introduce-landmark-legislation-that-takes-aim-at-greenwashing/ |access-date=24 September 2024 |work=Bucks County Beacon |date=18 July 2024}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Barton |first=Greg |title=Proposal Would Ban "Greenwashing" In PA {{!}} WDAC |url=https://wdac.com/proposal-would-ban-greenwashing-in-pa/ |access-date=2024-09-24 |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Sanders |first=Emily |title=How U.S. governments could crack down on greenwashing |url=https://www.exxonknews.org/p/how-us-governments-could-crack-down |access-date=2024-09-24 |website=www.exxonknews.org |language=en}}</ref>

On October 2, 2021, Rabb authored a memo to all members of the Pennsylvania House of Representatives indicating that he will be introducing legislation to enforce reproductive responsibility among men. According to the memo, the proposal would "require all inseminators to undergo vasectomies within six weeks from having their third child or 40th birthday, whichever comes first." Rabb's satirical<ref>{{cite web|last=Sadeghi|first=McKenzie|date=October 7, 2021|title=Fact check: Pennsylvania bill proposing restrictions on male reproductive rights is satirical|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/factcheck/2021/10/07/fact-check-legislation-male-reproductive-rights-parody-bill/6032780001/|access-date=October 9, 2021|website=USA Today}}</ref> memo was intended to draw attention to the double-standard of regulating women's bodies via legislation while the equivalent bill affecting men would seem absurd.<ref>{{cite web |title=House Co-Sponsorship Memoranda |url=https://www.legis.state.pa.us/cfdocs/Legis/CSM/showMemoPublic.cfm?chamber=H&SPick=20210&cosponId=36286 |website=The official website for the Pennsylvania General Assembly. |access-date=October 3, 2021 |language=English}}</ref><ref name="msn">{{cite web |title=3 Child Limit Bill Proposed in PA; Would Mandate Vasectomies |url=https://www.msn.com/en-us/news/politics/3-child-limit-bill-proposed-in-pa-would-mandate-vasectomies/ar-AAPauRy?ocid=msedgntp |website=MSN |access-date=October 5, 2021 |language=English}}</ref> Rabb called the memo "parody legislation".<ref name="msn"/>

In 2023, Rabb introduced bills to allow independent voters to vote in Pennsylvania [[primary election]]s (HB 979)<ref>{{cite news |url=https://penncapital-star.com/voting/pennsylvania-students-call-on-lawmakers-to-end-archaic-closed-primaries/ |title=Pennsylvania students call on lawmakers to end 'archaic' closed primaries |first=Cassie |last=Miller |work=Pennsylvania Capital-Star |date=October 16, 2023 |access-date=April 7, 2025 |id={{ProQuest|2877493431}} }}</ref> and to provide protections for [[cannabis]] consumers and businesses.<ref>{{cite news |title=The search to solve the cannabis conviction conundrum continues |last=Sweitzer |first=Justin |work=City & State Pennsylvania |date=November 27, 2023 |id={{ProQuest|2915672935}} }}</ref>

In 2025, Rabb entered the Democratic primary for [[Pennsylvania's 3rd congressional district]] to succeed Congressman [[Dwight Evans (politician)|Dwight Evans]] after he announced his retirement.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Terruso |first1=Julia |title=State Rep. Chris Rabb, an anti-establishment progressive, is running for Dwight Evans' Congress seat |url=https://www.inquirer.com/politics/philadelphia/chris-rabb-third-congressional-district-dwight-evans-democrat-20250708.html |access-date=4 December 2025 |work=The Philadelphia Inquirer |date=8 July 2025}}</ref> Rabb was endorsed by numerous [[Progressivism in the United States|progressive]] organizations and politicians, including the [[Justice Democrats]],<ref name="wfp">{{cite news |last1=Orso |first1=Anna |title=The progressive Working Families Party is backing State Rep. Chris Rabb for Congress |url=https://www.inquirer.com/politics/pennsylvania/chris-rabb-working-families-party-congress-20260319.html |access-date=19 March 2026 |work=The Philadelphia Inquirer |date=March 19, 2026}}</ref> [[Sunrise Movement]],<ref name="sunrise">{{cite news |last1=Orso |first1=Anna |title=Chris Rabb is trying to be the left's standard-bearer as he runs for Congress. Will progressives rally around him? |url=https://www.inquirer.com/politics/philadelphia/chris-rabb-progress-third-congressional-district-election-20260119.html |access-date=January 20, 2026 |work=The Philadelphia Inquirer |date=January 19, 2026}}</ref> [[Democratic Socialists of America]] (both the Philadelphia branch and the national organization),<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{cite news |last1=Walsh |first1=Sean Collins |title=Self-funding physicians, candidates trying to keep up, and a frontrunner: Inside the money race for a Philly congressional seat |url=https://www.inquirer.com/politics/philadelphia/congressional-race-fundraising-sharif-street-ala-stanford-20260202.html |access-date=February 3, 2026 |work=The Philadelphia Inquirer |date=February 2, 2026}}</ref> Congresswoman [[Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez]],<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-05-19 |title=Progressives seek another big primary win in the nation's bluest House district |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/2026-election/progressives-seek-another-big-primary-win-nations-bluest-house-distric-rcna344974 |access-date=2026-05-20 |website=NBC News |language=en}}</ref> and the [[Working Families Party]].<ref name="wfp"/> He joined the Democratic Socialists of America in 2026, but stated in an interview with ''[[Jacobin (magazine)|Jacobin]]'' that he has identified as a democratic socialist for longer.<ref name=":1">{{cite web |last1=Olla |first1=Akin |title=Philly Wants to Send a Socialist to Congress |url=https://jacobin.com/2026/05/rabb-pennsylvania-congress-socialism-class |website=[[Jacobin (magazine)|Jacobin]] |publisher= |access-date=15 May 2026}}</ref> [[American Priorities]], a pro-Palestine [[super PAC]] created to counter the influence of the pro-Israel [[AIPAC]], spent more than $400,000 in support of Rabb.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Strauss |first=Joseph |date=May 19, 2026 |title=With AOC backing and anti-Israel message, Chris Rabb wins primary in Philadelphia |url=https://www.jta.org/2026/05/19/politics/with-aoc-backing-and-anti-israel-message-chris-rabb-vies-for-open-house-seat-in-philadelphia |access-date=June 8, 2026 |work=[[Jewish Telegraphic Agency]]}}</ref> Rabb accused [[Ala Stanford]], one of his opponents, of receiving support from AIPAC, which both Stanford and AIPAC denied.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Cerino |first=Marco |date=April 6, 2026 |title=Third District congressional race intensifies amid PAC money disputes, endorsements and escalating political attacks |url=https://www.phillytrib.com/news/local_news/third-district-congressional-race-intensifies-amid-pac-money-disputes-endorsements-and-escalating-political-attacks/article_db6e52e8-59a7-4506-a65f-0cb2e68d825e.html |access-date=June 8, 2026 |work=[[The Philadelphia Tribune]]}}</ref> His candidacy was described as an example of a "[[Mamdanification|Mamdanified]]" campaign.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Platt |first=Larry |date=May 22, 2026 |title=The Mamdani-fication of Philadelphia |url=https://thephiladelphiacitizen.org/mamdani-fication-chris-rabb/ |newspaper=[[Philadelphia Citizen]] |access-date=6 August 2026}}</ref>

In December, Rabb's campaign Instagram account reposted a video promoting a theory that the [[2025 Bondi Beach shooting]] was perpetrated by "Zionists", which Rabb later disavowed and criticised, saying a former staffer was responsible for the repost.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Orso |first=Anna |date=May 1, 2026 |title=Chris Rabb disavows Instagram post suggesting Bondi Beach attack on Jews was false flag by 'Zionists' |url=https://www.inquirer.com/politics/philadelphia/chris-rabb-bondi-beach-post-20260501.html |website=The Philadelphia Inquirer |language=en}}</ref>

Rabb won the Democratic primary on May 19, 2026, defeating his opponents [[Sharif Street]], [[Ala Stanford]], and Shaun Griffith with 44% of the vote.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Orso |first=Anna |last2=Janesch |first2=Sam |date=2026-05-19 |title=State Rep. Chris Rabb wins Democratic primary for Philly congressional seat, a decisive win for the progressive left |url=https://www.inquirer.com/politics/philadelphia/chris-rabb-wins-third-congressional-district-philadelphia-primary-election-20260519.html |access-date=2026-05-20 |website=Inquirer.com |language=en}}</ref> He is running against independent candidate Dennis Mahoney in the general election.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Roth |first1=Fallon |title=Meet the humanitarian aid worker and independent candidate running against Chris Rabb in November |url=https://www.inquirer.com/politics/nation/3rd-district-election-dennis-mahoney-20260910.html |access-date=10 September 2026 |work=Inquirer.com |date=10 September 2026 |language=en}}</ref>

In September 2026, Rabb attended a protest ahead of a speech by Israeli prime minister [[Benjamin Netanyahu]] at the [[Eighty-first session of the United Nations General Assembly|United Nations General Assembly]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Speri |first=Alice |last2=McMenamin |first2=Lex |date=2026-09-24 |title=Netanyahu’s speech at UN spurs protests in New York City: ‘Let Gaza live’ |url=https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/sep/24/netanyahu-un-protests |access-date=2026-09-25 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Rabb has two sons and lives in East [[Mount Airy, Philadelphia|Mount Airy]].<ref name ="Meet"/> He is divorced from the scholar [[Imani Perry]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2009-02-26 |title=Demos Welcomes New Fellows Teresa Ghilarducci and Christopher Rabb |url=https://www.demos.org/press-release/demos-welcomes-new-fellows-teresa-ghilarducci-and-christopher-rabb |access-date=2026-05-20 |website=Demos |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Chris Rabb – Personal Democracy Forum |url=https://personaldemocracy.com/speaker/chris-rabb/ |access-date=2026-05-20 |website=personaldemocracy.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Perry |first=Imani |date=2024-11-13 |title=Digging in the Crates |url=https://imaniperry.substack.com/p/digging-in-the-crates |access-date=2026-05-20 |website=52 Curate}}</ref> Rabb identifies as [[nonreligious]] and was endorsed by the [[American Humanist Association]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Humanist, Atheist, Agnostic and Nonreligious Elected Officials |url=https://www.cfequality.org/secular-elected-officials |publisher=Center for Freethought Equality |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221224212536/https://www.cfequality.org/secular-elected-officials |archive-date=December 24, 2022 |access-date=May 12, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |author=Center for Freethought Equality |date=May 20, 2026 |title=Humanists and Atheists Flex Political Muscle as Chris Rabb Will Be First Person to Enter Congress As Openly Nonreligious |url=https://www.cfequality.org/issues/news/2026/5/20/humanists-and-atheists-flex-political-muscle-as-chris-rabb-will-be-first-person-to-enter-congress-as-openly-nonreligious |publisher=Center for Freethought Equality |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260626172204/https://www.cfequality.org/issues/news/2026/5/20/humanists-and-atheists-flex-political-muscle-as-chris-rabb-will-be-first-person-to-enter-congress-as-openly-nonreligious |archive-date=June 26, 2026 |access-date=May 12, 2026}}</ref>
